meta.title: Akamai, Betting the Cash Machine on AI
meta.dek: A security-and-delivery business that earned $1.5B of operating cash flow a year has signed $14B of seven-year contracts to rent out computers, and is spending $3.5B this year to build them. The stock has halved from May. What does $84 assume about whether the build pays?
meta.type: Distributed cloud and security platform: security, content delivery and cloud infrastructure services
meta.stage: Mid-pivot: a mature core funding a capital-heavy cloud build

verdict.sentence: The $14B of signed AI-cloud contracts are real and should add about $2.2B of revenue by 2028, but they earn roughly the hurdle at best-case pricing, and the probability-weighted case compounds at [[pw_return]] a year against the 13% hurdle.
verdict.breaks_if: Cloud infrastructure revenue is below about $180M a quarter by the Q2 2027 print, or the FY2027 cloud guide of $1.1–1.3B is cut, which would put the >$7.0B FY2028 revenue target out of reach.

call: Akamai has signed $14B of seven-year contracts to rent out compute, led by an $11.6B Anthropic deal, and the stock has gone from $165 in May to $84. I think that is roughly the right price, not a bargain. Management's own numbers put the after-tax return on those contracts at about 13%, and that is the floor price for the biggest customer, while capex this year is $3.5B against $1.5B of operating cash flow. Non-GAAP EPS of about $6.57 also leaves out roughly $3 a share of stock compensation, and owner earnings after SBC and capex fell from $657M in 2021 to $240M in 2025. To earn an ordinary 9% a year the stock needs [[Priced-in.eps]] of GAAP EPS in 2031, a shade above my Base of [[Base.eps]], and the price implies a Bear weight of about [[implied_bear]] against the [[Bear.prob]] I assign, so the market is slightly more optimistic than I am. No Bear weight, however small, earns 13% from $84, so the verb is Watch, and the case clears the hurdle at [[entry]]. The number that will settle it: cloud infrastructure revenue of about $180M a quarter by mid-2027, with non-GAAP operating margin stabilising in the mid-20s.

tests.claim: That the $14B of contracts ramp on schedule.
tests.test: Q4 2026 cloud infrastructure revenue of at least $120M (February 2027 print), the FY2027 guide of $1.1–1.3B held, and quarterly cloud revenue of at least $180M by the Q2 2027 print (August 2027).
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Bull to Bear (PW EV [[test1.pw_ev]], [[test1.pw_return]]/yr) → stays **[[test1.verb]]**, entry falls to [[test1.entry]]; a second slip also removes the $7.0B FY2028 target from my Base.

tests.claim: That margins bottom in the first half of 2027 and then expand.
tests.test: FY2027 non-GAAP operating margin guided at or above 24% in February 2027, and a GAAP operating margin above 9% in Q4 2027.
tests.if_fail: cut Base FY2031 GAAP EPS to about $5.50 from the model's Base (PW EV [[test2.pw_ev]], [[test2.pw_return]]/yr) → stays **[[test2.verb]]**, entry [[test2.entry]].

tests.claim: That the build is funded without a dilutive or downgraded financing.
tests.test: the $1.15B 0.375% notes due September 1, 2027 repaid from cash, no more than $2B of new debt or equity-linked paper raised through the FY2027 10-K, and no sub-investment-grade rating.
tests.if_fail: move 10 points from Base to Bear (PW EV [[test3.pw_ev]], [[test3.pw_return]]/yr) → **[[test3.verb]]**; the Outsider grade is cut to Anti-Outsider if buybacks resume while raising.

return_math.epv: $30–40 per share (five-year average owner earnings of $0.45B ÷ 9% ≈ $5.0B on 144M shares, about $35). Roughly 40% of the price pays for today's earnings power after SBC and capex; the rest pays for the contracts. The Bear ($42) sits just above EPV because it keeps the contracts but earns thin returns on them.
return_math.base_rate: The Base takes revenue from $4.45B to $8.2B, 13% a year nominal, roughly 10% real; for companies of $4.5–7B sales, 21% have done 10% real over five years, and ~16% a year to FY2028 is already guided and largely signed. The Bull (17% nominal, ~14% real) is a one-in-ten outcome for the size bucket.
return_math.year_ten: Mixed. The seven-year contracts end in 2033–34 and have to be renewed on hardware that is by then 7–10 years old; security still grows at year ten in the Base, delivery has shrunk by a third. The terminal multiple (18×) is below the market's for software and above it for infrastructure, so it is not carrying the value; the contract renewals are.
